chapter: The China offer, wedding and Shanghai
title: Food, honey wagons, Valaida Snow's cook and the White Russians
summary: He explains why they avoided Chinese vegetables, ate American food cooked by Teddy Weatherford's cook, and liked the White Russians.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What did you do about food then? Did you get everything?

We got every kind of food that we, we ate mostly food that came over on American boats. You see, because the Chinese they use human waste for fertilisers. Because I remember, I was riding a horse one day and fell in some of it. Way out in the country and my horse stumbled and I fell in it.
Well, they do that in Italy.
Do they?

Sure, haven't you ever seen the fields with all the toilet paper .....
.....
No, I didn't know that.

Well, another thing, in the morning if you are coming out of a club you can smell them coming for miles. They call them 'honey wagons'. And it's usually old women or old men, and they pick up these jars and dump it into the wagon. This is only in the poor Chinese section, not in the international center, no.
: Oh, I see.
And man, you can smell ledd 4+ that stuff! They just up and then they take it way out and put it over the vegetables.
So we didn't have any Chinese vegetables, not if we knew it. But it didn't bother them.
: Well, but, so that you didn't sort of eat Chinese food all the time?

Oh no. No, when we first got there we just liked the, we just, like we do here. You see, Teddy had one great big house over there that was his own. He had a Chinese fellow that Valaida Snow had taught how to cook American. Valaida had been over there before us.
: Oh she had?
Yes.
That was the girl that played trumpet?
Yes.
And sang?
Yes.
Used to be with Earl Hines or something?

Yes. She had been over there with another group and she had taught this, this Chinese cook how to cook anything American. So after she taught him Teddy kept him. And we ate just like, we didn't eat Chinese food. We ate a lot of rice, but we all liked rice, at least I did.
But didn't you once tell me too that there were a lot of White Russians there and ....
A lot of them, yes.
What about Russian food, did you get into that?
I ate it once or twice. I didn't like it too much. I didn't like that thick white cream they put over everything. I didn't like it. But we had a good time with the
Russians. I liked them. I liked them. They would tell me stories of the Revolution and how they were run out of Russia, Black Russia, what do they call it, Red Russians and Black Russians.
In fact, I was, I was learning to speak Russian a little bit before I left.
